neighbours.label: A due time is about to be stated for something owed: fires on the ' on' / ' the' right after 'due' or after handing work in ('homework on time', 'due on the first'), in assignment, rent and payment contexts; ' on' elsewhere and 'on time' for arrivals stay low.
fire: Every student is expected to hand in the lab report on time.
The second instalment of the fee is due on the last day of March.
Tenants must pay the rent on time or face a small charge.
Your final project is due on the Friday before the holidays.
She always turned in her worksheets on time, even when she was ill.
The library books are due on the date stamped inside the cover.
Please submit the signed permission form on time so your child can travel.
Membership dues are due on the first Monday of each quarter.
quiet: Every student is expected to bring a calculator to the lab.
The second instalment of the fee covers meals and transport.
Tenants must keep the stairs and the hallway clear.
Your final project should include a short list of sources.
She always wrote her worksheets in pencil, even in the exam.
The library books are shelved on the upper floor by subject.
Please put the signed permission form on the desk by the door.
Membership cards are printed on recycled plastic.

short: due time about to be stated
notes: Probe: 'hand in your essay on time' 0.76, 'Rent is due on the first' 0.86, 'after the deadline …' 0.48, 'Late work …' 0.30; 'on the table' 0.16, 'train arrived on time' 0.11. Near misses keep the school/rent topic and three keep an ' on', without any due time. The top examples also include the licence boilerplate 'distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS', which this label does not explain.
